parole.significato: A tree or plant that has been miniaturized by planting it in a small pot, restricting its roots, and by careful pruning.

parole.significato: The ancient Japanese art of creating miniature landscapes on black lacquer trays using sand and pebbles.

parole.significato: A very large bell used in Buddhist temples in Japan to mark time and call monks in for prayer.

parole.significato: A Japanese subculture associated with customized motorcycles and riding together in large groups.

parole.significato: A Japanese sweet made by soaking sweet rice and forming it into balls with azuki bean paste packed around them.

parole.testo: Reportedly coined in reference to the extremely muscular character Broly from the Dragon Ball anime franchise, with the suffix -ic. parole.significato: The heavy collision of the two rikishi during the tachiai at the start of a sumo bout.

parole.significato: A practitioner of budo.

parole.significato: A Japanese traditional courtly dance, with slow, regal movements.

parole.significato: To climb Mount Fuji during the night, in order to see the sunrise at the peak.

parole.significato: A Shinkansen train; a Japanese high-speed rail train.

parole.significato: A Japanese written language established mainly during the Heian period, circa 900–1200 C.E., and commonly used until ci…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Japanese 文(ぶん)語(ご) (bungo, “writing language”).

parole.significato: A traditional form of Japanese puppet theatre.

parole.significato: A Japanese dish consisting of a bowl of rice topped with braised or grilled pork; pork donburi.

parole.significato: A type of soup or cooking stock, often made from kelp.
